memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From there they continued on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together and I will give them water." Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing about it, about the well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people sank—the nobles with sceptres and staffs." Then they went from the wilderness to Mattanah. - Num 21:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the grumbling over water earlier in the journey, here is a refreshing change. God promises water at a place called Beer, and this time the people respond not with complaints but with a song.

What a difference gratitude makes. The same need that once produced bitter murmuring now produces joyful singing. The water was a gift from the Lord, and Israel received it with thanksgiving, even celebrating the ordinary work of digging the well. Worship transformed the moment.

This teaches us something about the posture of our hearts. The circumstances of the wilderness had not fundamentally changed, yet the people had a choice in how they responded. They could grumble, or they could sing. This time, they chose the song.

We face the same choice daily. When God meets our needs, do we simply move on, or do we pause to give thanks? A grateful heart turns provision into praise and finds joy even in the desert. In Christ we have living water that never runs dry (John 4:14), and that alone is reason enough to sing. Let gratitude, not grumbling, be the melody of your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you respond to God's provision with gratitude or with grumbling?
2. When did you last sing to God simply out of thankfulness?
3. How can you cultivate a more grateful heart this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, turn my grumbling into gratitude and my complaints into song. Thank You for the living water I have in Jesus that never runs dry. Amen.
